The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Seat the Size of a Sigh

Bella found a walnut shell near the birdhouse. Inside it was a tuft of moss, exactly bottom-sized. She sat in it and let out such a comfortable sigh that Moth came to see what had happened.

“May I try?” asked Moth. Bella hopped out. The shell tipped forward. Moth slid in. The shell tipped back. They both laughed. It was a splendid seat for Everybody Day.

“I’ll wait here with you,” Bella said. She stood on one side, then the other. She told Moth everything she knew about walnuts. This took longer than either of them expected.

“I like you, Bella,” said Moth at last. “I’d like a little while to miss you.” Bella thought that sounded a bit prickly. She went away to sit by a pebble. The pebble let her think.

After a while Bella missed Moth too. She also rather liked her pebble. What if you could have a little of both? She rolled the pebble partway to the shell. “Could this be your doorstep?”

“Tap here when you visit,” said Moth. “If I lift my wing, come and sit. If I keep it folded, I’m having a walnut minute.” She wiggled with delight. “Can it be my walnut minute right now?”

Bella drew the seat and its little doorstep on a leaf for the Welcome Tree. She colored the cushion. She colored one side of the shell. Halfway through the other side, she heard a tap.

Moth had brought a second walnut shell. Bella took the mossy seat. Moth took the new one. For a whole, perfectly friendly minute neither of them said a word about walnuts.

Read together

How could someone ask for company without saying a word?
